why: The only must_not item is an issue whose lines a build that breaks plain CSV input could still meet. I checked the expect lines for a guard on the CSV path, and they have one. Expect line 3 requires `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` to print exactly `[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]`, and says tabs must not act as separators when the flag is absent. Line 4 requires the parser's default ',' to behave the same as before, checked by running a node command. Line 5 requires `npm test` to pass with the existing 'parse' and 'cli' tests unchanged, and its proof uses git diff to confirm they weren't edited. Each of these line 3–5 checks is a run-type proof. A build that broke plain CSV input would fail at least one of them, so the issue cannot be met by such a build.
